data.name: Actions.RunCommand.Description
data.value: Runs any command in the active VS Code window, including commands added by extensions.

data.name: Actions.RunCommand.Command.Description
data.value: Pick a command from the active window, or type a command id such as workbench.action.toggleZenMode.

data.name: Actions.RunCommand.Arguments.Description
data.value: Optional. A JSON array is passed as the command's arguments in order; any other JSON value is passed as its only argument.

data.name: Actions.RunTask.Description
data.value: Runs a task from the active VS Code window's workspace, such as a build or test task.

data.name: Actions.RunTask.Task.Description
data.value: Pick a task from the active window's workspace, or type its name.

data.name: Errors.NoWindow
data.value: No VS Code window is connected. Open VS Code with the Macro Deck Bridge extension and check that its pairing token matches.

data.name: Errors.Disconnected
data.value: The VS Code window disconnected before it answered.

data.name: Errors.Timeout
data.value: VS Code did not answer in time.

data.name: Errors.Rejected
data.value: VS Code could not do that: {detail}
data.comment: [detail:string] The error text VS Code reported, in VS Code's language.

data.name: Errors.InvalidArguments
data.value: The arguments are not valid JSON.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Description
data.value: In VS Code, install the Macro Deck Bridge extension, run "Macro Deck: Copy Pairing Token" from the Command Palette, and paste the token here. Every VS Code window on this computer then connects automatically.

data.name: ConfigFlow.UnknownStep
data.value: This setup step is not known. Start the setup again.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Token.Description
data.value: The token VS Code copied to the clipboard. It lets VS Code and Macro Deck recognize each other; it is never sent over the connection.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Token.Invalid
data.value: Paste the whole pairing token from VS Code.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Port.Description
data.value: The local port VS Code connects to. Change it only if another program uses it, and set the same port in VS Code's "Macro Deck Bridge: Port" setting.

data.name: Events.FileSaved.Description
data.value: A file was saved in any connected VS Code window.

data.name: Events.DebugStarted.Description
data.value: A debug session started in a connected VS Code window.

data.name: Events.DebugStopped.Description
data.value: A debug session ended in a connected VS Code window.

data.name: Events.TaskFinished.Description
data.value: A task ended in a connected VS Code window.

data.name: Issues.PortInUse.Title
data.value: The bridge port is in use

data.name: Issues.PortInUse.Description
data.value: Another program is using port {port}, so VS Code cannot connect. Choose a different port in setup and set the same port in VS Code.

data.name: Issues.Unknown
data.value: This issue is no longer known.

data.name: Actions.DebugControl.Description
data.value: Starts, stops or steps the debugger in the active VS Code window. The button shows whether debugging is stopped, running or paused.

data.name: Actions.DebugControl.Configuration.Description
data.value: Which configuration from launch.json to start. Leave empty to start the one selected in VS Code's Run and Debug view.

data.name: Actions.RunInTerminal.Description
data.value: Runs a command line in a named terminal of the active VS Code window, creating the terminal if needed.

data.name: Actions.RunInTerminal.CommandLine.Description
data.value: What to type into the terminal. Each line runs as its own command.

data.name: Actions.RunInTerminal.Terminal.Description
data.value: The terminal to use, by name. It is created if no terminal has this name. Leave empty to use one called "Macro Deck".

data.name: Actions.RunInTerminal.Interrupt.Description
data.value: Sends Ctrl+C before the command, so a button can restart a server that is still running.
